title: Inbound/outbound token-rate experiment with soft commitments
creator: Priya Singh
description: Run a controlled field experiment that splits per-token metering into separate inbound (client-provided prompt/context) and outbound (generated tokens) rates with an optional soft commitment layer for enterprise contracts. The goal is to measure behavioral changes, revenue impact, and operational burden compared to our current single-rate model and to validate contract language that allows graduated grace credits instead of hard penalties for falling below committed usage. This ticket covers experiment design, contract wording draft, telemetry instrumentation, and a pilot with 6 enterprise customers over 4 weeks.
acceptance_criteria: Experiment matrix defined with at least three variants (baseline single-rate, split-rate parity, split-rate discounted-outbound)
Instrumented metrics and dashboards for token ingress, token egress, streaming sessions, and billing delta
Runbook for customer-facing questions and automated invoice reconciliation in place
Legal and Sales approval for proposed soft-commit contract language
Pilot completed with 6 customers and initial analysis run (N>=100k tokens per customer)
steps: Draft experiment plan and win/loss criteria (PM + Finance)
Design A/B variants and mapping logic in billing service (ENG)
Draft soft-commit contract language and SQ implications (Legal + Sales)
Select and onboard pilot customers (Solutions & CSM)
Run 4-week pilot, collect data, and synthesize results
notes: Rationale: many enterprise workloads are output-heavy (long generations) — splitting rates may better reflect unit economics and reduce sticker shock for prompt-heavy customers
Tradeoff: split metering increases billing complexity and support surface; soft commitments reduce churn risk but complicate revenue recognition
Technical concern: streaming sessions need per-stream accounting to avoid double counting prefix tokens when reconnecting — implementation must be idempotent
We should avoid introducing new minimums in pilot customers' invoices; use internal trial credits to simulate commitment breaches

decisions: Adopt a conservative pricing delta for outbound tokens in the pilot (-10% list) to lower friction for generative-heavy customers
Implement soft-commit grace credits that amortize over a 30-day window rather than immediate penalties
Do not surface split-metering on invoices during pilot; use internal reporting to evaluate impact

impact_estimate: Model projection: +1.8% revenue lift from better-aligned outbound pricing, with estimated +0.7% churn risk mitigated by soft-commit credits
